newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cotton crop not damaged by Hurricane Danny.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cotton crop not damaged by Hurricane Danny.

text.p: Cotton crops throughout the Southeast U.S. were spared damage from Hurricane Danny, which brought much-needed rain to some areas of the Cotton Belt, industry sources said.
"Ultimately, Danny was considered a non-event for cotton," said Mike Palmerino, a meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
The storm did not produce enough rain in the cotton-growing areas to damage crops in most areas because it is early in the season and bolls remain closed.
"It's awfully difficult to hurt cotton with rain unless the bolls are open," Palmerino said.

The heaviest rains fell over Alabama and struck hardest at the southwestern part of the state. While heavy winds from the hurricane blew fruit off some of the crops, there is enough time left in the season for crops to recover, said Charlie Burmester, a cotton specialist in Alabama.
"Damage is going to be fairly minimal to cotton crop in Alabama," Burmester said, adding that rain in the northeastern part of the state will benefit the thirsty crop.
Heavy rains fell in North Carolina from the remnants of the hurricane, but the storm remained west of the cotton-growing areas.

In Georgia, the storm did not bring enough rain to provide relief to the parched crops, Steve Brown, a cotton specialist, said. "We needed a broad rain across the state but we didn't get it. The hurricane did not adversely affect us at all."
